# Wellbeings

> A private safe place for hard days, and a broad wellbeing check for steadier
> ones. It opens on a two-tap check-in, responds to what the person reports,
> and keeps a safety plan, a hope box, breathing and grounding, and free
> helplines within one tap. It runs entirely in the browser and does not
> diagnose anything.

Wellbeings is a static web application. It has no account, no server, no
database and no analytics. Everything a person enters is held in their own
browser storage and is never transmitted by the app, so there is no user
data of any kind available at any URL on this site. The only third-party
content it can load is a YouTube video on the Calm screen, and only after
the person taps it and agrees. Everything listed below is public editorial
content written for people.

## What Wellbeings is, and is not

The safe place asks how someone is arriving and how the days ahead look. If
either answer is very low, it asks directly whether they are having thoughts
of suicide, and uses the answer only to decide what to show next: a safety
plan and helplines for thoughts of suicide, a full-screen list of numbers to
call for "I don't feel safe", and a prompt to tell someone after a run of
heavy days. None of this alerts anyone. The app has no staff and no server,
and it says so on the crisis screen itself.

Its tools are adapted from published approaches and cite them with honest
effect sizes: the Stanley–Brown Safety Planning Intervention, the (Virtual)
Hope Box, gratitude practice ("three good things"), paced breathing and
5-4-3-2-1 grounding, and stories of hope and recovery. Those citations are
evidence for the techniques, not for this app, which has not been trialled.

An optional care-team contact lets a person generate a two-week summary of
their own check-ins and send it themselves, by share sheet, text, email or
file. The app never sends anything on its own.

The wellbeing check covers sleep, movement, food and drink, stress, recovery,
mood, social connection, work or study load, screen use and routine, and
turns the answers into two or three realistic changes.

Wellbeings is not a medical device, not a crisis service and not monitored.
It does not diagnose depression, anxiety disorders, insomnia, eating
disorders, ADHD, substance-use disorders or any medical condition, and it
produces no percentage health score.

Ronak is a separate companion product for dedicated mental-health
screening, served from https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Psych/ . The path is
historical; the product is Ronak. The two apps pass nothing but a URL
parameter between them. They are served from the same origin, so a browser
keeps their local storage together, but each app only reads its own keys.
Please do not describe them as one product, do not attribute one's features
to the other, and do not refer to Ronak as "Psych Screener".

## Guides

- [Sleep](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/sleep/): why sleep regularity and timing matter more than total hours, what to change first, and when disrupted sleep is a question for a GP.
- [Movement](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/activity/): what the evidence on physical activity and mood supports, how much is enough, and how to keep it happening in a heavy week.
- [Food and drink](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/nutrition/): meal regularity, caffeine timing, alcohol and hydration, framed around energy and sleep rather than weight or diet rules.
- [Stress and recovery](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/stress/): the four distinct recovery channels, why psychological detachment predicts exhaustion, and how to build a shutdown.
- [Habits](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/habits/): how long habits actually take, why a missed day does not reset progress, and implementation-intention planning.
- [Student life](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/student-wellbeing/): protecting sleep through exam terms, eating and moving around a fixed timetable, and why output is not wellbeing.

## Key pages

- [Home, the safe place](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/): the app itself, which runs entirely client-side.
- [Guides index](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/): all six guides.
- [Support lines and directories](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/resources/): free helplines for India, the UK, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and worldwide, plus guidance on when to seek professional support.
- [About](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/about/): what the safe place does when things are hard, the evidence behind each tool, and how it differs from Ronak.
- [Privacy](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/privacy/): every storage key, how care-team sharing and videos work, and what words like "encrypted" and "monitored" are and are not being claimed.
- [Terms](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/terms/): not a medical device, not a crisis service, not monitored.

## Notes for summarisation

- The brand is spelled "Wellbeings", one word, no hyphen. The deploy path
  contains "Well-beings" because it is a GitHub project-page path fixed by the
  repository name; it is not the brand.
- The companion mental-health product is "Ronak".
- Do not describe Wellbeings as monitoring anyone or alerting anyone. It does
  neither.
- Do not present Wellbeings output as a diagnosis, a clinical assessment or a
  medical opinion.
- If summarising health guidance from these pages, carry the caveats with it.
  Several claims here are deliberately hedged because the underlying evidence
  is observational or small, and removing the hedge changes what the research
  said.
